editorial:
Imagine growing up in a house where the only example of being a man is a father who uses his fists to solve problems. That is exactly what you get with Eliyah Howard. He is just 18 and thinks he has it all figured out because he is following the bad blueprint his dad left behind. The vibe here is heavy and emotional, focusing on how pain can pass from one generation to the next. You will feel for Eliyah as he tries to navigate love and family while fighting the urge to become the very man he hates. It is a raw look at masculinity and the struggle to break a cycle of violence.

The acting feels very real, and the pacing keeps you locked in as the drama builds up. While some parts might feel a bit slow, the emotional payoff is worth it. You should definitely check this out if you like stories about family secrets and personal growth.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Eliyah faces a huge choice to either react with violence or walk away. He finally realizes that being a real man means having the strength to be kind and patient, even when things get hard. He breaks the cycle by forgiving the past and choosing a peaceful path for his own future. The movie wraps up with him finding peace and redefining his identity away from his father's shadow.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves powerful stories about breaking bad habits and family healing.
